internal.title: Incident Resolved: Elevated Error Rate in Checkout Service Due to Payment Service Flag Misconfiguration
internal.body:
At 10:21 UTC on 2026-11-08, an alert was triggered for a high error rate in the checkout service. Initial diagnosis identified a 50% error rate in the payment service caused by an erroneous flag configuration ('paymentFailure') that injected errors by invalidating payment tokens.

The flag was disabled at 10:41 UTC after approval, leading to a rapid recovery with error rates returning to normal levels shortly thereafter.

Root Cause: A recent change enabled the 'paymentFailure' flag at 50%, causing payment request failures and cascading errors in the checkout service.

Resolution: The flag was promptly disabled, restoring normal service operation.

Lessons learned include the importance of cautious flag deployment and rapid rollback procedures for error injection flags.

Timeline:
- 10:21 UTC: Alert received for high error rate in checkout.
- 10:41 UTC: Diagnosis confirmed payment service error injection due to flag.
- 10:41 UTC: Flag disabled after approval.
- 10:41 UTC: Recovery verified with normalized error rates.

external.title: Some checkouts failed due to payment processing issues
external.body: Between 10:21 and 10:41 UTC on 2026-11-08, some customers experienced failures completing checkout due to issues in the payment processing system. The issue was identified and resolved by disabling a misconfigured feature flag that was causing payment errors. Normal service resumed shortly after the fix was applied. We apologize for any inconvenience caused.

output.impact: Customers experienced failures completing checkout during the incident window due to payment processing errors.
output.root_cause: A feature flag ('paymentFailure') was set to 50%, injecting errors by invalidating payment tokens in the payment service, causing cascading failures in checkout.
output.resolution: The problematic feature flag was disabled promptly after diagnosis, restoring normal service operation.

lessons.lesson: Exercise caution when enabling error injection flags; ensure thorough validation and monitoring to prevent widespread impact.
lessons.applies_when: When error injection flags are enabled in the payment service.

lessons.lesson: Monitor downstream service flags and error rates closely to quickly identify cascading failures affecting checkout latency and error rates.
lessons.applies_when: When payment service error rates are elevated, potentially impacting checkout service.

action_items: Implement stricter controls and automated checks for enabling error injection flags.
Enhance monitoring dashboards to correlate flag changes with service error rates in real time.
